scenario: AITA for dumping food on my girlfriends plate at a wedding until it was overflowing? | Me and my girlfriend are moderately overweight. We have been noticing that we were getting fatter still, so I pushed us to try and lose some weight. We now go on walks everyday, we cut the sugar and generally try to eat better and in reasonable quantities. This is being tougher on her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I'm mainly the one trying to keep us on track and very often I have to call her out when she's sliding back into our old eating habits. So this last weekend we went to a wedding together as guests. We were sitting next to each other, together with family members from both our families, all in the same table. Every table had its own food so everyone could just serve themselves. So what happened next was I had to watch as my girlfriend filled her plate up with all kinds of delicious food. I kinda gave her a look like that, but she just shrugged it off as if to say "yeah I know, but we're at a wedding". I was slightly annoyed with her behavior but sort of forgot about it and tried to just enjoy everyone's companies. Some time after that, when she was finished, she was out for more. She asked me to pass her this big plate of shrimp rice so that she could try some of that. That really struck me, but I didn't want to argue right there and then, so what I did was get the srino rice and proceed to fill her plate up until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She just kind of stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me at this point and I thought it was better I just went outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line and they I came off as a controlling jerk. So, am I the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregard for our agreed upon diet?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. My girlfriend and I have been trying to lose weight because we noticed we were getting heavier. We've been walking every day, cutting sugar, and eating better and in reasonable quantities. It's been tough for her because she really enjoys eating until she's full. I've been the one trying to keep us on track, and I often have to call her out when she's slipping back into our old eating habits. Last weekend, we went to a wedding together with family members from both our families. Everyone was sitting together at the same table, and each table had its own food so people could serve themselves. I watched as my girlfriend filled her plate with all kinds of delicious food. I gave her a look, but she just shrugged it off, saying, "Yeah, I know, but we're at a wedding." I was slightly annoyed but tried to enjoy everyone's company. Later, when she finished, she asked me to pass her a big plate of shrimp rice so she could try some of that. That really bothered me, but I didn't want to argue right there. Instead, I took the shrimp rice and proceeded to fill her plate until it was literally overflowing a little bit. She stared at it, then got up and went outside alone. Everyone was staring at me, and I thought it was better to go outside too to talk to her. She told me she was humiliated and that I stepped out of line, acting like a controlling jerk. Now, I'm wondering if I was the asshole for taking a stand against her completely disregarding our agreed-upon diet. First, I need to consider the context. We're at a wedding, which is a social event where people often enjoy food. It's a celebration, and it's normal for people to eat more than usual. However, we have a mutual agreement to try to lose weight, which involves eating in reasonable quantities and cutting sugar. I tried to call her out by giving her a look, but she dismissed it, saying it's a wedding. That shows she's aware of our agreement but chose to disregard it in this specific situation. Later, when she asked for more food, I reacted by overfilling her plate, which led to her feeling humiliated and upset. I need to evaluate whether my reaction was appropriate or if it crossed a line into being controlling or disrespectful. On one hand, I was trying to hold her accountable for our agreed-upon goals. On the other hand, my method of filling her plate until it overflowed was confrontational and likely hurtful. I should also consider the setting. We were at a wedding with family members from both our families. My actions drew attention to ourselves, which could have been embarrassing not just for her but also for me and our families. Moreover, the way I chose to address her behavior was through a public display of control, which can be seen as manipulative or dominating. Instead of having a private conversation about her eating habits, I made it a spectacle, which likely contributed to her feeling humiliated. It's also important to think about the dynamics of our relationship. I've been the one pushing for accountability, but it's crucial to maintain respect and understanding. Disagreements about diet and lifestyle choices can be sensitive, and it's essential to approach them with empathy and open communication. In this case, my reaction was impulsive and confrontational, which led to a negative outcome. It would have been better to address the issue privately, expressing my concerns without making a scene. This way, we could have had a constructive conversation about our goals and how to handle situations like this in the future. Additionally, recognizing that weddings and other social events are times when people often indulge a bit more, it might be reasonable to allow some flexibility within our diet plan. It's about finding a balance between maintaining our goals and enjoying social interactions. In summary, while I was trying to uphold our agreed-upon diet, my method of addressing her behavior was inappropriate and hurtful. It crossed the line into being controlling and disrespectful, making me the asshole in this situation.
